column1: # Per-shot parity gate thresholds for tools/parity/compare.ps1 -Gate.
# Format: name <TAB> min_ssim <TAB> max_mean_abs_diff
# These are tolerances, not equality: retail (1997 D3D via dgVoodoo2, or software) and the port
# (Bevy) are different renderers, and the port's HUD is inside its frame while the retail world
# crop has none. A *verified* pose pair currently scores 0.62-0.63 SSIM here, so the floors sit
# just under that: a real camera or draw regression is caught (moving the level-1 eye by 0.03
# units drops the pair to ~0.24), while renderer/HUD noise is not.
# Raising a floor is the right move when a renderer change improves a pair; lowering one needs
# a reason in the commit message. A pair captured without a row here is reported as UNGRADED.
# The numbers are tied to the capture policy in tools/parity/port-capture.ps1: 600 frames
# (`--frames 600`), the window sized from the retail sidecar, and whatever renderer
# retail-capture.ps1 used (16-bit D3D via dgVoodoo2 by default). Changing either side's
# framing or frame count invalidates them.
# route_catwalk and route_door are captured but intentionally not gated: retail's reference there
# shows a scripted red screen tint that ramps in over the 1 s series (a position-triggered effect),
# while a port capture with `--shot-at` only moves the camera and leaves the player at the level
# start, so its scripts never fire. They are triage rows until the port can warp the player (Phase
# 0.5), and their measured 0.46/0.41 is the size of that difference, not a renderer tolerance.
